reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. Write H_j for the unnormalized probabilists' Hermite polynomial of degree j, with its integer coefficients interpreted in R (H_0(t)=1, H_1(t)=t, and H_(n+1)(t)=t H_n(t)-n H_(n-1)(t) for n>=1). Define Phi_j(w)=[x |-> H_j(<w,x>)] in L^2(gamma_E; R), where brackets denote the almost-everywhere equivalence class of the literal square-integrable function displayed. For every j in N={0,1,2,...} and every w in E, let r_(j,w):E -> R be the representative function obtained by coercing Phi_j(w) from L^2 through its almost-everywhere-function class to a function. Then r_(j,w)(x)=H_j(<w,x>) for gamma_E-almost every x in E. On the right, the integer-coefficient Hermite polynomial is evaluated in R using the canonical integer-to-real algebra map. The almost-everywhere quantifier lies inside the quantifiers over j and w; the assertion does not require a common exceptional null set for all w, and it does not assert equality at every x.
objects: The L^2 feature Phi_j(w), its coerced representative r_(j,w), and the literal Hermite evaluation function.
domains: j in N; w and x in E; both compared functions are E -> R; exceptional sets measured by gamma_E.
quantifiers: For every E, every j in N and every w in E, for gamma_E-almost every x, r_(j,w)(x)=H_j(<w,x>).
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product structure and Borel measurable structure only; w need not have unit norm.
conclusion: Almost-everywhere equality of the coerced representative and the Hermite evaluation function.
scopes: Equality is gamma_E-almost everywhere in x for each fixed j,w, not pointwise and not a simultaneous all-w assertion outside one specified null set.
constant_dependencies: The representative and possible exceptional set may depend on E,j,w. The Gaussian depends on the inner-product structure of E. No free numerical constants occur.
semantic_notes: The double coercion is from an L^2 element to its AEEqFun class and then to a representative function.
Polynomial.aeval evaluates the integer-coefficient Hermite polynomial into R; it is not evaluation in an unspecified coefficient field.
